article.title: Tidal Is Deleting, Rejecting, and Banning Fully AI-Generated Music

blocks.text: This year we introduced Tidal’s AI Policy to protect artists and keep listeners informed. Since then, we’ve been identifying, labeling, and demonetizing tracks we determined are 100% AI generated outputs of tools like Suno, Lyria, and more.
But that’s not enough. We think a more drastic change is in order. Here’s what we’re updating today, and why.
Starting December 9, any wholly AI-generated track that's submitted to Tidal will be rejected and removed from our platform.

Over the past 90 days, 43% of all tracks distributed to the platform have been detected as wholly AI-generated. These tracks have been labelled for listeners and removed from the royalty pool. On November 6, we had the greatest influx of AI music yet: Over 60% of the deliveries we received were wholly AI generated. Today, approximately 27 million tracks in our catalog are tagged as such, representing 6.3% of all available music on Tidal. Yet Tidal subscribers are not listening to these tracks: 96% of them have received zero streams in the last three months.

Wholly AI-generated music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists is another serious problem that has only increased in scale: It diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans. To date, we’ve taken down over 65,000 tracks flagged for suspected artist-name impersonation.

It’s true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. But this situation is different – at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried.

To ensure Tidal remains the best place for artists to share their work, and for listeners to enjoy it, we’re removing all tracks that we determine are 100% AI generated. We’re also banning distributors from delivering these tracks to us, and will reject deliveries if their metadata says they were generated solely using AI tools. Tracks that were assisted by AI tools, but not the sole outputs, will be allowed on the platform.

Our AI policy was designed to provide a great experience for listeners, while protecting the authenticity and livelihoods of artists and rightsholders. Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more. Everything in this update comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for, or copied by someone pretending to be you. We’ll keep sharing what we find and we’ll keep acting on it.
Enforcing our policy is made possible with technology provided by ⁠Ircam Amplify, our AI detection partner.
